requirements.title: Assumed business name registration
requirements.agency: Montana Secretary of State, Business Services
requirements.quote: A person transacting business in this state under an assumed business name shall register with the secretary of state, on forms furnished by the secretary of state, an application for registration of the assumed business name
requirements.notes: The Secretary of State's fee sheet (sosmt.gov/business/fees) lists $20 to register and $20 to renew, and a registration lasts 5 years (MCA 30-13-204).

requirements.title: City of Bozeman business license (home-based location)
requirements.agency: City of Bozeman Community Development, Business Licenses
requirements.quote: Business licenses are required for occupations, professions, enterprises, and establishments which are conducted for profit on any premises in the City of Bozeman, not exempted by state law or Chapter 12 of the Bozeman Municipal Code.
requirements.notes: A home-based license is applied for through ProjectDox with a  fee and a signed Home-Based Business Acknowledgement Form and renews every 12 months for ; the fire-safety inspection on the page applies to commercial locations.

requirements.title: Home-based business standards and acknowledgement (BMC 38.360.140)
requirements.agency: City of Bozeman Planning / Community Development
requirements.quote: Any individual applying for a business license, with the intent of operating the business from such person's home, shall acknowledge by signature such person's understanding of the requirements and conditions of this chapter.
requirements.notes: Conditions include running the business inside the dwelling (not an accessory structure), using no more than 25% of the floor area, no outside storage, and at most one on-premises half-time nonresident employee.

requirements.title: Cottage food operation registration
requirements.agency: Gallatin City-County Health Department, Environmental Health Services
requirements.condition: Required to sell as a cottage food operation (from home, at farmers' markets, bazaars or other in-person venues); not required if every sale is made under the Montana Local Food Choice Act, or if selling only at farmers' markets.
requirements.quote: Do not begin selling cottage food products until your registration has been reviewed and approved by the Gallatin City-County Health Department.
requirements.notes: One-time $40 fee (re-register if moving or adding recipes or labels); submit recipes with ingredient weights, a label for each product and water-source documentation to ehs@gallatin.mt.gov, as MCA 50-50-117 requires registration with the county health authority.

requirements.title: Cottage food product labels
requirements.agency: Montana DPHHS (enforced by the local health authority)
requirements.condition: Applies to cottage food products, and to containered food sold at farmers' markets under 50-50-121(6), unless sold under the Montana Local Food Choice Act.
requirements.quote: package cottage food products and label the cottage food products prior to sale, including on the label, at a minimum, the following:
requirements.notes: The label needs the operation's name and full address, product name, ingredients in descending order by weight, net quantity, allergens, and the statement "Made in a home kitchen that is not subject to retail food establishment regulations or inspections." in at least 11-point type.

requirements.title: Cottage food sales limits (direct, face-to-face, in Montana)
requirements.agency: Montana DPHHS (enforced by the local health authority)
requirements.condition: Applies when selling as a registered cottage food operation.
requirements.quote: "Direct sale" means a face-to-face purchase or exchange of the cottage food product between the manufacturer or packager of a cottage food product and a consumer or individual purchasing the cottage food product as a gift.
requirements.notes: No consignment, shipping, internet sales, sales to stores or restaurants, or sales outside Montana; the statute sets no annual dollar cap on sales.

requirements.title: Montana Local Food Choice Act sales (alternative to cottage food registration)
requirements.agency: Montana DPHHS (guidance); no registering agency
requirements.condition: Only if the owner sells homemade food under the MLFCA instead of registering as a cottage food operation.
requirements.quote: a producer shall inform an end consumer that any homemade food or homemade food product sold through ranch, farm, or home-based sales pursuant to this part has not been licensed, permitted, certified, packaged, labeled, or inspected
requirements.notes: Sales must be directly to an informed end consumer, for home consumption or at a traditional community social event such as a farmers' market, and only in Montana; no state or local license, registration or labeling may be required.

requirements.title: Gallatin farmers' market vendor application
requirements.agency: Gallatin City-County Health Department, Environmental Health Services
requirements.condition: If selling at farmers' markets under the farmers'-market exemption (MCA 50-50-121) rather than as a registered cottage food operation or under the MLFCA; confirm with the health department.
requirements.quote: Do not begin selling food products until your application has been reviewed and approved by the Gallatin City-County Health Department.
requirements.notes: There is no fee; DPHHS's farmers' market guidance says market managers keep records of food vendors except those with a DPHHS license or Cottage Food Registration.

requirements.title: Temporary food event license
requirements.agency: Gallatin City-County Health Department, Environmental Health Services
requirements.condition: Only if food is prepared, cooked, served open or sampled at the market or event.
requirements.quote: A temporary event license may be required when food is prepared, cooked, served, or sampled at a temporary event or market.
requirements.notes: Selling sealed, labeled jars and packaged baked goods does not by itself call for one; offering samples needs a temporary handwashing setup.

requirements.title: Retail food establishment or wholesale food manufacturing license
requirements.agency: Montana DPHHS / Gallatin City-County Health Department
requirements.quote: A cottage food operation that meets the requirements in this section is not a retail food establishment or a wholesale food establishment and is not subject to licensure or inspection requirements under Title 50, chapter 57, or this chapter.
requirements.notes: A food license would be needed only to sell to stores or restaurants, out of state, or to make foods outside the approved cottage food list (for example, refrigerated or low-sugar jams).

requirements.title: Food safety training or certified food protection manager
requirements.agency: Montana DPHHS / Gallatin City-County Health Department
requirements.quote: Fill out the application and include the required recipes, labels, and water documentation.
requirements.notes: Neither MCA 50-50-116/117 nor Gallatin's registration steps call for a food safety course or certificate; this verdict rests on those listed requirements rather than an explicit statement.

requirements.title: Montana sales tax registration
requirements.agency: Montana Department of Revenue
requirements.quote: Montana does not have a general-use sales tax.
requirements.notes: No sales tax to collect on jam or baked goods and no sales tax account to open.

requirements.title: Local resort tax
requirements.agency: Montana Department of Revenue (informational); local resort communities
requirements.quote: Before collecting resort tax revenue, the Montana Department of Commerce must first designate a community (incorporated) or area (unincorporated) as a resort community or area (7-6-1501, MCA).
requirements.notes: Bozeman is not on the department's list of resort areas (Red Lodge, Virginia City, West Yellowstone, Whitefish, Big Sky, Cooke City, Craig, Gardiner, St Regis, Wolf Creek) and is far above the 5,500 population limit for a resort town.

requirements.title: Business equipment (personal property) tax reporting
requirements.agency: Montana Department of Revenue
requirements.quote: Businesses whose statewide market value of equipment is $1 million or less are exempt from the business equipment tax.
requirements.notes: No report is due unless new property pushes the value over the threshold or the department asks for one.

requirements.title: Weighing device (scale) license
requirements.agency: Montana Department of Labor & Industry, Weights and Measures Bureau
requirements.condition: Only if a scale is used at the point of sale to set the price by weight.
requirements.quote: According to Montana statutes all weighing or measuring devices used commercially in the State of Montana must purchase an annual license from the Weights & Measures Bureau through the E-stop licensing system.
requirements.notes: Kitchen scales used to weigh ingredients are not 'commercial', so jars and baked goods sold by the unit need no scale license.

requirements.title: Bozeman mobile vending license
requirements.agency: City of Bozeman Community Development
requirements.condition: Only if selling from a vehicle, sidewalk cart, trailer or similar mobile unit.
requirements.quote: Mobile vending units include motorized vehicles, sidewalk carts, trailers, and other mobile contraption offering goods for sale
requirements.notes: Not needed for a farmers' market booth or in-person sales from home, which the regular business license covers; the mobile vending license costs $250.

requirements.title: Employer Identification Number (EIN)
requirements.agency: Internal Revenue Service
requirements.quote: You need an EIN if you: Have employees
requirements.notes: No employees and no excise taxes, so the owner can use a Social Security number; an EIN is optional for banking.

requirements.title: Workers' compensation coverage
requirements.agency: Montana Department of Labor & Industry, Employment Relations Division
requirements.quote: Unless the employer elects coverage for these employments under this chapter and an insurer allows an election, the Workers' Compensation Act does not apply to any of the following: ... (d) employment of sole proprietors
requirements.notes: With no employees, no workers' compensation policy, unemployment insurance account or state withholding account is needed; hiring would change this.

requirements.title: FDA food facility registration
requirements.agency: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
requirements.quote: The private residence of an individual is not a facility.
requirements.notes: A home kitchen selling directly to consumers does not register with FDA.

requirements.title: FDA acidified food process filing
requirements.agency: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
requirements.quote: Carbonated beverages, jams, jellies, preserves, ... are excluded from the coverage of this part.
requirements.notes: Standard jams and jellies need no acidified-food registration, process filing or Better Process Control School.

requirements.title: FDA Nutrition Facts label
requirements.agency: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
requirements.quote: Food offered for sale by a person who makes direct sales to consumers (e.g., a retailer) who has annual gross sales made or business done in sales to consumers that is not more than $500,000
requirements.notes: Exempt while labels and advertising make no nutrition claims; ingredient, allergen and net quantity labeling still apply under the state cottage food rules.

requirements.title: Montana individual income tax and estimated payments
requirements.agency: Montana Department of Revenue
requirements.quote: If you estimate you will owe more than $500 in tax for last year, you should make quarterly estimated payments this year.
requirements.notes: Business profit is reported on the owner's Montana individual income tax return.

requirements.title: Federal self-employment tax and estimated tax payments
requirements.agency: Internal Revenue Service
requirements.quote: Individuals, including sole proprietors, partners, and S corporation shareholders, generally have to make estimated tax payments if they expect to owe tax of $1,000 or more when their return is filed.
requirements.notes: Profit is reported on Schedule C and Schedule SE with Form 1040.

hard_calls.about: Cottage food registration vs. the Montana Local Food Choice Act
hard_calls.explanation: Montana offers three lawful routes for home-made jam and baked goods: register as a cottage food operation ($40, labels, face-to-face sales); sell under the MLFCA with no registration or label but a required disclosure to an informed end consumer, for home consumption or at events like farmers' markets; or sell only at farmers' markets without registering (50-50-121). Because Bridger Jam also sells directly outside markets, the cottage food registration is the usual route, but it is not strictly required if every sale fits the MLFCA.

hard_calls.about: Gallatin farmers' market application for registered cottage food operators
hard_calls.explanation: Gallatin's farmers' market page asks vendors to file a (free) application before selling, but does not say whether a vendor already registered as a cottage food operation must also file; DPHHS guidance exempts cottage food registrants from market record-keeping. Private markets may also impose their own requirements.

hard_calls.about: City business license for a homemade-food seller
hard_calls.explanation: The MLFCA bars state and local agencies from requiring licensure that pertains to preparing or selling homemade food, and Bozeman exempts businesses 'exempted by state law'. The city's general business license is not food-specific, so the key treats it as required, but no official source addresses this overlap.

DPHHS's cottage food FAQ (file named 2024) is dated February 2018 and its guidance March 2020; Gallatin's page (updated July 2026) adds a water-source document not in statute. The Gallatin City-County Health Department publishes on healthygallatin.org (not .gov), and Bozeman's and the Secretary of State's sites refused automated fetches, so they were read in a browser.
